quarterly_data.signal: Record quarter across the board: first time about $12 billion of orders in one quarter (+28% comparable, broad-based, no pre-buy pattern seen); record revenues of $9.5 billion (+12% comparable, price ~2%); Operational EBITA up 20% to $1.9 billion with margin up 90 basis points to 20.2%; gross margin 40%; book-to-bill positive at 1.27 in all three business areas; income from operations and EPS both up 8%; free cash flow $881 million. Orders up double digits in all regions: Americas +52% like-for-like (US +62%, base orders +~30%), Europe +12%, Asia/Middle East/Africa +12% (China +10%).
quarterly_data.figure: Orders about $12 billion (+28%); revenue $9.5 billion (+12%); Operational EBITA $1.9 billion (+20%), margin 20.2%; book-to-bill 1.27; EPS +8%; FCF $881 million

quarterly_data.signal: Electrification surged: comparable orders +58%, topping the $7 billion mark for the first time (after first ~$5B in Q4 and ~$6B in Q1); sixth consecutive quarter of positive book-to-bill, at 1.39; order backlog +59% to $13.7 billion; group backlog at a record $30 billion (+28% comparable). DATA CENTERS again the standout with a TRIPLE-DIGIT order increase — yet even excluding data centers Electrification orders still grew double digits. Electrification revenue $5.2 billion (+19% comparable), Operational EBITA +26% to $1.3 billion at a record 24.9% margin. Customer mix unchanged (hyperscalers vs colocation similar) — 'the whole segment is running faster'; significant data-center wins also in Europe and Asia this quarter. Backlog deliveries extend beyond 2027 into 2028, including some data centers. Management: gained market share in data centers at least since Q1; strong position in medium-voltage UPS.
quarterly_data.figure: Electrification orders +58% to above $7 billion (first time); data-center orders +triple digits; EL backlog $13.7 billion (+59%); group backlog $30 billion; book-to-bill 1.39

quarterly_data.signal: Full-year 2026 guidance RAISED: comparable revenue growth now expected at low double-digit to low teens (from high-single-to-low-double); Operational EBITA margin to improve from 2025 even excluding the Q1 real-estate gain. Q3 guide: low to mid-teens comparable revenue growth with sequential margin improvement (Electrification revenue growth at least similar to Q2 with margin improving from 24.9%; Motion mid-to-high single digit; Automation mid-single digit). Free cash flow to improve from 2025's $4.6 billion. Pricing +~2% in the quarter, strongest in the Americas; price-cost gap to be more than compensated by year-end.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 comparable revenue growth raised to low double-digit to low teens; Q3 low to mid-teens; FCF to improve from $4.6 billion

quarterly_data.signal: 800V DC data centers: 'We have ZERO order in the backlog for 800 volt DC data centers. Nobody has, because there is waiting for the availability of components from NVIDIA and the like.' Commercial impact seen from late 2027 or 2028 onwards; ABB building the complete 800V DC portfolio now — already a leading player in DC switches, breakers and components, expects the new architecture to shift more content to medium voltage, boosting its medium-voltage UPS. Heavy R&D allocation plus the announced acquisition of Advantics (France — DC technology, silicon carbide technology, joining Electrification for DC and data center). Dedicated DC-topic webcast announced for September 24.
quarterly_data.figure: Zero 800V DC orders in backlog industry-wide; commercial opportunity late 2027/2028; Advantics acquisition adds DC/SiC technology

quarterly_data.signal: Motion orders reached $2.6 billion (+20% comparable), rising sequentially against the usual seasonal trend, with strength in grid stabilization (industry-leading synchronous condensers), rail, marine, mining, HVAC for commercial buildings and DATA CENTER COOLING. ABB positions as the COMPONENT PROVIDER to the cooling industry: 'We are partnering with all of the major cooling companies in the world who delivers those air cooling or large chiller units that sits in the data centers today' — supplying drives and motors, and in liquid cooling the pumps that push liquid to the rack. Motion revenue $2.2 billion (+4%); margin 18.5% (-130bps: Gamesa Electric dilution ~70bps, High Power inefficiencies to resolve in H2).
quarterly_data.figure: Motion orders $2.6 billion (+20%); revenue $2.2 billion (+4%); margin 18.5%

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity is the governor of order intake: 'We do not take orders where we aren't fully committed that we can deliver on time.' Guidance raised because capacity from previous years' investments is now coming online with the expected benefits; multi-year CapEx build-out across the US, China and India, plus a newly announced $200 million expansion and additional CapEx into Europe. Continuous expansion 'especially in Electrification, every unit that we have with more square meter, more Robotics, more Automation and more people'. Lead times unchanged — order strength reflects real demand, not lead-time extension or pre-buying.
quarterly_data.figure: $200 million additional European capacity CapEx announced; capacity additions in US, China, India

quarterly_data.signal: Announced offer to acquire Rotork, a leading independent manufacturer of actuators (electric actuators more than half of sales), at GBP 5.03 per share — about $5.5 billion in USD terms (EV/sales ~5.3x, EV/EBITDA ~19.5x 2025, mid-teens with synergies). Rotork 2025 revenue GBP 777 million at a 24.6% adjusted operating margin; would add ~3% to ABB revenues and ~12% to Automation revenues, run as a separate division. Actuators are also needed in data-center cooling applications and nuclear power. Close expected H1 2027. Two smaller deals: Specialtrasfo (medium-voltage transformers, Italy) and Hoglund (marine automation).
quarterly_data.figure: Rotork offer GBP 5.03/share (~$5.5 billion); Rotork 2025 revenue GBP 777 million, 24.6% margin
